chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I buy something from the tax collector (or official), and I know that he is unjust (overcharging/taking more than due).' He said: 'Buy it from him.'

key_terms.الْعَامِلِ: The official or tax collector (often referring to the Imam's representative or governor)
key_terms.يَظْلِمُ: He is unjust (specifically in the context of overcharging or taking more than due in trade)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy from an unjust official or tax collector in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the transaction even if the buyer is aware of the official's injustice, emphasizing that the validity of the sale (*sahih*) is independent of the seller's moral or financial misconduct. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between the validity of the contract and the separate issue of the official's accountability for their oppression. It provides practical guidance for consumers in administrative contexts, ensuring that market stability is not disrupted by the individual faults of officials.
